title: Population and Settlements: How People Fill the Earth

questions.question: The world's population reached 8 billion in:
questions.rationale: The United Nations marked 8 billion in November 2022, eleven years after the 7-billion milestone of 2011.

questions.question: Although billions arrive ever sooner, the rate of world population growth:
options: Peaked around the late 1960s and has since fallen below 1%
questions.rationale: Growth peaked above 2% per year around the late 1960s and has slowed to under 1% — still rising in total, but more slowly.

questions.question: In stage 2 of the demographic transition model:
options: Birth and death rates are both low
Birth rate stays high while death rate falls fast
questions.rationale: Early expanding: modern medicine and food cut the death rate while the birth rate stays high, producing rapid population growth.

questions.question: Japan and Germany, with birth rates below death rates, illustrate which DTM stage?
questions.rationale: Stage 5 countries see deaths outnumber births, so population shrinks despite development.

questions.question: About what share of humanity lives in Asia?
questions.rationale: Asia holds roughly 60% of the world's people, with about 4.8 billion of the 8 billion total.

questions.question: Which became the world's most populous country, passing China around 2023?
questions.rationale: India (about 1.43 billion) overtook China (about 1.41 billion) around 2023 to become the most populous country.

questions.question: All of these are sparse regions because of harsh conditions EXCEPT:
questions.rationale: The Ganga plain's water, level fertile land, and cities make it one of Earth's densest regions; the others repel settlement.

questions.question: Which of the following is a PULL factor in migration?
questions.rationale: Pull factors such as jobs, safety, and services attract migrants; war, persecution, and crop failure push them out.

questions.question: According to India's 2011 Census, the sex ratio was:
questions.rationale: The 2011 sex ratio was 943; Kerala's 1,084 was highest, Haryana's 879 lowest, and the child sex ratio 919.

questions.question: Compact, nucleated villages are most typical of:
questions.rationale: Where fertile soil and water coincide — as on the Ganga plain — homes cluster together; hills and forests force dispersed settlement.
